content.thinking:
I'm tracing the root cause to revision 26f1d7e, which removed the month-total update inside record_purchase, so total_this_month_cents never gets updated regardless of the feature flag. That explains why shopper month totals fail to reconcile for the affected users.

Every write path adds only to total_cents without moving the stored month total, which reconcile then compares against actual in-month purchase sums — cites S1, U4, U5. The deploy of 26f1d7e at P2.1 removed the conditional month-total addition from record_purchase for the path where derive_the_month is off, and all three replicas were running it by T13.1; the earlier P1 deploy can't be ruled out cleanly since there's no health metric from the hour before onset, but AL1's oldest affected purchase at 21:30 on Oct 18 falls after P2's 21:28 deploy, pointing to it as the trigger.

Checking T16, no flag changes by anyone but Argus occurred in the hour before onset, so a flag flip isn't the trigger. The alert's 7-day check window and the 21:30 Oct 18 oldest-affected timestamp line up almost exactly with that boundary, suggesting the corruption started right around when the check could first catch it rather than earlier.

So the real mechanism is that the revision removed the month-total increment from record_purchase, the only write path, while statement, summary, and reconciliation code (U1-U3, U6) kept reading that stored field as truth, per S1's docstring explaining why it exists. The root cause is that commit 26f1d7e deleted that write path without removing the dependent readers.

Since S1 and D1 directly confirm this without needing further tracing, this does qualify as a reached cause. As for contributing factors, I'm noting that nothing appears to validate the stored month total against actual purchase sums, and reconciliation only runs weekly, so the drift went undetected for an extended period.

For CF-2, I'm checking whether any test at the time of the revision actually tied record_purchase to the readers of total_this_month_cents. F1 points to tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py at commit 26f1d7e on main, and its findings apply to what actually ran — the new test cases fail against the current record_purchase_deriving_the_month implementation, suggesting no existing test caught the removed write.

AI-1's fix adds tests but only along the deriving path, not the record_purchase path at the running revision where F1 was written against main's still-adding behavior. Deploying main with the fix should make both paths add the total correctly though.

For CF-3, nobody was paged since the alert didn't tie to any on-call incident — otherwise someone would have triggered the rollback and repair. The action is to page on-call for SpendTotals.

CF-4: I'm checking whether the dormant deriving-path behaving the same way before the change is actually a contributing factor — but since record_purchase was the one modified, the fallback path doesn't change the outcome, so I'll skip it as not contributing, though F1's fix still addresses it.

CF-5: request-level metrics stayed flat because that kind of monitoring can't detect this sort of data corruption in the first place.

On rollback, reverting io-shop to the earlier commit restores the addition on the non-deriving path but leaves the deriving path still broken, so rollback alone doesn't fully mitigate — that gap becomes its own action item. For remediation I'm drafting an action item to run the repair script from the PR against the account store, first in report mode and then with the write flag, before the month rolls over.

Other mitigation ideas: checking whether any monthly statements or spend summaries were rendered from the short totals since onset and finding those out, since the record doesn't show this. For detection, I'm proposing running the reconciliation job on a much shorter cadence than before, and paging on-call whenever the reconciliation mismatch alert fires.

For prevention, I want a test confirming that a recorded purchase leaves reconciliation clean when going through the off-path (derive-the-month disabled), since existing tests only cover the on-path. I also want a process requiring a review of all readers of a stored field before removing any write to it. Separately, I notice the deployed revision isn't actually present in main's history, which is itself a notable contributing factor — a deploy bypassing main.

I should probably simplify this into a factor noting that no test or review caught the mismatch between the write path and the still-reading consumers, while the deployed revision apparently isn't in main's history. The real ongoing risk is that the running code keeps writing each purchase without updating the stored month total, so every additional purchase this month makes more shoppers' totals increasingly short.

For what went well, Argus correctly held off acting without verification, and Code-Fix responded with a draft PR containing a fix, tests, and a one-off repair script. I want to describe what was proposed concretely rather than vaguely characterizing it.

For went_wrong, the Investigator's candidates only named record_purchase, missing that record_purchase_deriving_the_month also corrupts the running total — meaning the recommended rollback wouldn't actually stop damage for shoppers on that path. That's a genuine gap, plus the fact that nobody got paged. For got_lucky, I'm noting that customer-facing revenue was unaffected even though stored figures were corrupted internally.

As for assumptions, I'm flagging that I'm inferring stored totals reach customers via statements based on U1-U3 and U6 without seeing actual rendering, and that it's unclear whether affected shoppers were actually on the derive_the_month=false path.

Framing the cause in plain language: a software update broke the running-total tracking for the month, which other shop systems still depend on, without naming any numbers. For the causal chain, I'm citing the deployment evidence and replica state, then tying it to the earliest affected purchase shortly after the change, while ruling out alternative explanations like pre-onset flag changes. I need to make sure the final prose has no raw numbers or PR references, replacing them with citation markers instead.

action_items.item: Run the one-off repair script from Code-Fix's draft pull request against the account store before the month rolls over: first in its default report-only mode, then with --write once the report has been checked.
Find out which monthly statements and spend summaries were produced from the short month totals since the onset, and whether any reached shoppers.

Make sure any rollback or fix that is deployed also covers the derive_the_month path. At the revision being rolled back to, record_purchase_deriving_the_month also leaves the month total unchanged, so rolling back alone stops new damage only for purchases recorded with derive_the_month off.
Run reconcile_monthly_totals on a schedule much shorter than {A5} days, or after writes, so drift between stored totals and purchases is found soon after it starts.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
Add a test that recording a purchase through record_a_purchase with derive_the_month off leaves an account in which reconcile_monthly_totals finds nothing wrong.
Require review to list the readers of a stored field (such as total_this_month_cents) before a change stops writing it, and require deployed revisions to come from reviewed history on main.

causal_chain.step: The stored monthly spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them: {A1} of the {A2} shopper totals checked did not reconcile, the widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}. The statement and spend-summary code reads that stored total. No error rate was measured, and the shop's takings did not fall by more than they normally vary.

Every purchase recorded since then was written without updating the stored month total. At the running revision, both write paths (record_purchase, and record_purchase_deriving_the_month, which record_a_purchase picks between) add the price only to total_cents. The reconciliation check compares the stored month total with the sum of this month's purchase prices, so each purchase this month opens a gap the size of its price.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after the later deploy of 26f1d7e.
A flag change just before the onset: the flag provider's history shows {T16.2} changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, took the conditional month-total addition out of record_purchase, the path used when derive_the_month is off. The path used when it is on already left the month total unchanged, so after this change no path updated it. As of {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas ran this revision. The oldest affected purchase, at {A4}, comes after this deploy.

The change broke the service because it stopped writing a field that other code still reads. The new docstring says the month figure will be added up from purchase history whenever it is wanted. But the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation code still read total_this_month_cents directly, and the module itself says the running totals exist so that pages do not have to sum a shopper's whole history. Nothing changed those readers.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed how purchases are recorded so that the shop stopped updating each shopper's running total for the month, but other parts of the shop still read that total as if it were current.

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing seen watching for stored totals drifting from purchases was the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The request-level series stayed flat because the service kept serving normally.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check run more often would have found the gap soon after the deploy, before most of a week's purchases were written short.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or review was seen that would catch a write path no longer updating a field that statement, summary and reconciliation code still read. Code-Fix reports that the deployed revision is not in main's history.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The change would have been stopped before it was deployed, even though it still dropped the month-total update.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been asked straight away to roll back and repair the totals, rather than the recommendation waiting to be noticed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: The alert fired before the month rolled over. According to Code-Fix's reading, the repair depends on the in_current_month marks on stored purchases still describing the damaged month, and a later onset in the month could have pushed discovery past that point.
went_well: The Investigator read the diff of the suspect deployment {T12.1 - alert_raised} after the alert. That diff showed directly that the month-total update had been removed.
Code-Fix proposed a fix, new tests and a one-off repair script as a draft pull request {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert.
went_wrong: Neither candidate noticed that at the running revision record_purchase_deriving_the_month also leaves the month total unchanged. The recommended rollback therefore would not stop new damage for purchases recorded with derive_the_month on.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e took the month-total addition out of record_purchase, so that no write path still moves total_this_month_cents: record_purchase_deriving_the_month already left it unchanged. The change rests on the idea that the month figure can be worked out from purchase history whenever it is needed, but the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation code all still read the stored field. Each purchase this month therefore leaves that field short by the purchase's price.
input.still_at_risk: The running revision still records every purchase without updating the stored month total, so each new purchase this month adds to the shortfall that statements and spend summaries read, and the totals already written stay wrong until a person rewrites them; Code-Fix's reading says that rewrite has to happen before the month rolls over.
input.symptom: Shoppers' stored spend totals for the month fell behind the purchases they made
